11six24-pegasus-jelly-bean-2: Soft, dense feel with quick hands and easy dinks; some find put-away power modest.
11six24-ultre-jelly-bean-2: Plush control on dinks, drops and resets, but a few found it head heavy and slow in hand battles.
11six24-ultre-power-2: Spin, pop and a large sweet spot; a good number find the feel stiff and muted.
11six24-vapor-power: Easy power and a big sweet spot with little adjustment; some found the stiff feel hard on the arm.
11six24-vapor-power-2: Durable grit gives plenty of spin, but dead spots along the top edge are a common complaint.
bread-butter-loco-hybrid: Heavy spin and fast hands for attackers, though the pop makes dinks and resets hard for some.
crbn2-trufoam-genesis: Spin and a big sweet spot with a dense feel; the main complaint is durability, with a few rattling.
crbn3-trufoam-genesis: Dense, consistent feel for an easy soft game, though many find it head heavy and short on power.
enhance-duo: Control, spin and a big sweet spot, and several own the widebody as their main paddle.
honolulu-j6cr: Spin and pop with a big sweet spot; the grit is inconsistent and wore smooth within months for some.
luzz-cannon: Often compared favourably with a Joola Perseus Pro IV for less; the power can be hard to control.
pickleball-apes-pulse: Soft control on drops and dinks that improves after break-in; several report core crush.
ronbus-quanta-r3-16: Great-value power and pop that works best with weight added; edge guards coming loose is the gripe.
ronbus-quanta-r4-16: Fast in the hands with plenty of power, but it feels light stock and edge guards come loose.
rpm-jade-elongated: Softer feel with easy drops and dinks, though a few were lukewarm on its power next to the Ultré.
six-zero-black-opal-14mm: Easy power and spin for centred hits; the small sweet spot makes resets and volleys tougher.
six-zero-coral-16mm: Forgiving resets and dinks for players leaving poppier paddles; edge guards separating is the gripe.
six-zero-coral-pro-16mm: Grit that spins well and lasts, and it suits kitchen players; many report dead spots near the top.
six-zero-ruby: Plush feel with easy resets and dinks; the main gripe is grit wearing smooth after several months.
spartus-spitfire-elongated: Spin and drive power, and many call it their main paddle; some find it too poppy for touch shots.
vatic-pro-prism-flash: Soft, forgiving first paddle at a low price, but it lacks power and the grit wears off in months.
vatic-pro-saga: Plush, Prism-like feel with more power; a couple found it weak or nothing special.
vatic-pro-v-sol-pro: Budget paddle with good control and easy pop, a clear step up on the Prism Flash; the grit fades.
vatic-pro-v-sol-tour: Spin, power and pop, a step up from the V-Sol Pro; many saw the face go smooth within weeks.
